courses.name: Data Mining and AI
courses.description: Builds predictive models using data mining and machine-learning techniques for business decisions.
courses.prerequisites: (VSB 2020 or SBI 3040) and VSB 2008 and (VSB 2009 :Y or SBI 3020)

category_review.rationale: Machine-learning algorithms and predictive modeling are central stated subject matter.

courses.name: Decision Analytics & AI
courses.description: Combines data mining, decision models, programming, and generative AI to solve business problems.

category_review.rationale: The current description explicitly integrates generative AI and data mining in decision analytics.

courses.name: Intro to Econometrics
courses.description: Applies stochastic methods, estimation, hypothesis tests, regression, and time-series analysis to economic relationships.
courses.prerequisites: (ECO 1001 or SBI 2005) and ECO 1002 and (STAT 1235 or STAT 1313 or STAT 1430 or STAT 4310 or VSB 2005)

category_review.rationale: Statistical estimation, regression and probabilistic methods are the course subject; no AI method is established.

courses.name: Applied Financial Statistics
courses.description: Uses probability, financial time-series models, panel data, and regression-based statistical methods.

category_review.rationale: Financial context does not change the explicit statistics/econometrics subject.

notes: The course description explicitly states: Class does not count as Finance elective. This limits use toward a Finance companion major; co-major option membership is retained.

courses.name: Advance Data Mining & AI
courses.description: The current description discusses management theory, motivation, leadership, discipline, and organizational culture.

category_review.rationale: The AI title contradicts the management-theory description. Source identity/description conflict prevents a reliable single category.

notes: Current official title and description have divergent subject cues; the source body is recorded as published, without repairing the catalog by inference.
The current course description requires junior or senior standing, in addition to the separately stated MGT 3170 :Y prerequisite. The :Y notation is preserved without interpretation.

courses.name: Sports Analytics
courses.description: Uses R and analytics for sports evaluation, scouting, and in-game decisions.

category_review.rationale: Description centers on sports-domain analytical applications, without an explicit AI methodology.

courses.name: CRM and Data Analytics
courses.description: Studies CRM data infrastructure, warehouses, information cubes, reporting, and business-intelligence technologies.
courses.prerequisites: VSB 2006 and (VSB 2020 or SBI 3040) and (VSB 2009 or SBI 3020)

category_review.rationale: Data warehousing and business information systems are the explicit technical center; data mining is one included technique.

courses.name: Database Management
courses.description: Studies database models, SQL, distributed databases, and client/server database technology.
courses.prerequisites: VSB 2006 and (VSB 2020 :Y or SBI 3040) and (VSB 2009 :Y or SBI 3020)

category_review.rationale: Database implementation and data management systems are systems content.

courses.name: Business Intelligence with AI
courses.description: Examines business-intelligence processes and pipelines using a generative-AI perspective.
courses.prerequisites: VSB 2006 and (VSB 2020 or SBI 3040) and (VSB 2009 or SBI 3020)

category_review.rationale: The source centers business-intelligence concepts, processes and tools and an end-to-end Modern Data Stack pipeline, viewed through generative AI. It does not establish a primary AI model/method curriculum, so systems and AI content remain mixed.

courses.name: Marketing Analytics
courses.description: Applies marketing analytics using JMP, web analytics, advertising tools, and Excel.

category_review.rationale: The source emphasizes marketing decision tools and practice, without specific AI methods.

notes: The source description literally states: Maximum of 5 VSB minors. Its meaning is not established; no individual eligibility or minor-count interpretation is inferred.

courses.name: Programming in R & Python
courses.description: Introduces R and Python programming fundamentals, assisted by AI, with business analytics libraries.

category_review.rationale: Programming-language fundamentals are primary; AI assists learning and business applications.

notes: The undergraduate co-major substitution names this course Programming in R & Python; the current graduate catalog heading is Programming with AI. Applicability across these labels/versions remains unconfirmed.

courses.name: Data Models & Struct Analysis
courses.description: Studies structured business data models, database analysis, and reporting methods.

category_review.rationale: Structured databases and data models support a systems classification.

courses.name: Business Intelligence
courses.description: The current description covers optimization, probability, and simulation modeling for business decisions.

category_review.rationale: Despite the Business Intelligence title, the actual description names optimization/probability/simulation as its subject.

notes: Current official title and description have divergent subject cues; the source body is recorded as published, without repairing the catalog by inference.

courses.name: Principles of Database Systems
courses.description: Studies relational databases, queries, normalization, physical organization, and a database implementation project.
courses.prerequisites: (CSC 1051 or ECE 1620 or ECE 1260) and (CSC 1300 or MAT 2600)

category_review.rationale: The description directly establishes database management and implementation.

requirements.title: Local program requirements
requirements.summary: Complete the local curriculum and applicable policies below. Published amounts are credits; credit-system normalization remains unverified.

requirements.title: Analytics and AI electives
requirements.summary: Choose the published number of electives, subject to the alternative and substitution policies below.

requirements.title: Required primary major
requirements.summary: The BBA co-major requires a primary major in Accounting, Economics, Finance, Management, Management Information Systems, Marketing, or Real Estate.

requirements.title: Major overlap
requirements.summary: At most one co-major course may also satisfy another VSB major.

requirements.title: Database alternative
requirements.summary: The elective listing provides MIS 3050 or MIS 2030 as one three-credit option; they are not two independent elective slots.

requirements.title: Other approved electives
requirements.summary: Catalog exposes an Other Approved Electives entry with no listed courses or approval procedure. This unresolved entry prevents a complete inventory.

requirements.title: Joint program eligibility
requirements.summary: The following graduate-course options apply to students pursuing both Analytics and AI and the MSBAi program.

requirements.title: Graduate elective
requirements.summary: For eligible joint-program students, MSA 8105 may satisfy one Analytics and AI elective.

requirements.title: Graduate substitutions
requirements.summary: For eligible joint-program students, one additional listed substitution may count: CSC 4480 or MSA 8110 for MIS 2030; only one of these three courses may count. Alternatively, MSA 8240 may replace MIS 3060; only one of that pair may count.

requirements.title: Graduate permission
requirements.summary: Undergraduates need department, graduate-program and undergraduate-program permission for up to nine graduate credits. Graduate-program application requires relevant approvals. Courses must be taken while undergraduate; they cannot be applied retroactively after degree conferral.

requirements.title: Graduation GPA FAQ
requirements.summary: VSB requires cumulative, technical (all business courses), and major GPAs of at least 2.0 for graduation. This records the published GPA applicability without claiming the entire BBA is mapped.

requirements.title: Additional Information: school-wide letter-grade and S/U rules
requirements.summary: The current VSB catalog Additional Information applies letter grading to major courses; S/U is permitted only for non-business or free electives. Co-major coursework cannot use S/U as a major requirement.

requirements.title: MIS 3050 or MIS 2030: one elective slot
requirements.summary: If this elective slot is selected, choose MIS 3050 or MIS 2030; the two courses cannot fill two of the three elective slots.

notes: A co-major within the BBA requiring a primary VSB major; award other preserves the nonstandalone BBA relationship. Official directory specifies Class of 2029 and beyond, not a launch date.
Local program inventory only; does not certify the host BBA degree. Credits are source amounts; credit-unit normalization is unverified. Pool subtotals are not required totals.
Other Approved Electives modal is empty. Neither its membership nor approval rule is verified, so the co-major remains partial.

2026-10-11: The live Other Approved Electives modal still contains only the label Total Credits. The official program page links to a test catalog host whose robots policy disallows retrieval. No list or open-ended approval rule was obtained; no alternate-host bypass or live/test curriculum merge was attempted. The primary parser now rejects newly populated modal content for review.

All 14 represented course descriptions were reread. Prerequisites preserve source notation, including :Y, without inventing its meaning. Graduate course records use current undated graduate-catalog descriptions while preserving the undergraduate substitution labels and explicit version limits.
